never_do.because: Elastane loses its recovery permanently above about thirty degrees. Nothing looks damaged afterwards — the garment simply stops springing back and never fits the same way again. A garment that is mostly something else is still governed by its small elastane content.

never_do.never_do: Don't wring it out, and don't hang it up wet.
never_do.because: This fibre loses much of its strength when wet. Wringing sets permanent creases and hanging lets the garment stretch under the weight of the water it is holding. Press the water out between towels and dry it flat.

never_do.never_do: Don't dry it in direct sunlight.
never_do.because: Ultraviolet light breaks down dye faster than it damages fibre, so the garment fades long before it wears out — and it fades unevenly, along whatever line was facing the sun.

impact_estimate.energy_note: A cold cycle. Most of a wash cycle's energy goes on heating water, so a cold one uses substantially less and sheds less fibre.
impact_estimate.method: Relative, not absolute, and it applies only if the garment is washed. Fibre class from the matrix, weighted by composition, then shifted by construction and finish per the published shedding research cited on each rule. It ranks garments against each other rather than measuring any of them. Note that this counts fibre released, not microplastic released — cotton and wool shed heavily too, and those fibres are not persistent in the way synthetic ones are.

unknowns: What this garment needs may be more than can safely be done to it at home, and it has no professional route recorded. The gentler option is taken deliberately; repeat it rather than escalating.
